picks.title: Nearly 40% of music released last month used AI
picks.excerpt: A SubmitHub study found AI involvement detected in nearly 40% of music released in July, with almost a quarter fully AI-generated. It's the clearest data yet on how fast generative tools have entered everyday release workflows.
picks.rationale: Hard numbers on how far AI has already spread into normal release workflows — the baseline every other music-AI argument now has to start from.

picks.title: Round Hill sues Suno and Anthropic for up to $1bn apiece — and isn't looking to settle
picks.excerpt: Publisher Round Hill has filed separate copyright suits against Suno and Anthropic seeking up to $1bn each, with statutory damages of up to $150,000 per work willfully infringed. It says it isn't looking to settle — a counterweight to the wave of licensing deals.
picks.rationale: The one Suno-cluster pick: a publisher refusing to settle reopens the training-data question just as licensing looked like the settled answer.

picks.title: OpenTune is a free, open-source AI pitch correction tool
picks.excerpt: OpenTune is a free, open-source AI pitch-correction tool for Windows and macOS — a Melodyne/Auto-Tune-style alternative built on a neural approach. Still in beta, and currently Chinese-only in the UI.
picks.rationale: Most immediately actionable item in the pool: a free neural alternative to the most expensive fixed cost in a vocal chain, downloadable today.

picks.title: Alibaba launches AI song generator HappyShrimp 1.0 in beta, with Taihe Music signed up for artist co-creation
picks.excerpt: Alibaba has launched HappyShrimp 1.0 in beta, an AI song generator whose prompts can specify instrumentation, vocal style and how a track's energy shifts across its running time. China's Taihe Music has signed up for artist co-creation.
picks.rationale: A big-tech rival to Suno arriving with a label partner attached, and prompt control over arrangement and energy curve rather than just genre.

picks.title: The best ethical AI music plugins: six tools that license their training data
picks.excerpt: LANDR, Moises AI, Voice-Swap and more: a roundup of six AI music tools that license their training data and share revenue with the artists behind it. A practical guide for producers who want AI in the chain without the ethical debt.
picks.rationale: The practical answer to the litigation story above — a named shortlist of AI tools whose training data is licensed and revenue-shared.
